intent: Give a freshly installed machine a working escape hatch from the hosts file-guards. Until now --rollback refused to run on exactly the machines the previous commit created.
scope: Follow-up to 4c426eae, which made hosts-blocker's install.sh register the guard-lib instances directly.
Non-goal: changing what the migration path records; a migrated machine keeps its existing legacy backup and restore behaviour unchanged.
changes: do_rollback no longer exits when /var/lib/guard-lib-migration is absent. That state dir is written by the one-shot migration, but a machine set up by hosts-blocker's install.sh has no legacy layer to back up and therefore no state dir -- so --rollback bailed out while the very instances it exists to remove were live. It now proceeds whenever a guard-lib instance is registered, warns that there is no legacy layer to restore, and still refuses when there is genuinely nothing to roll back.

After uninstalling the instances, re-assert chattr +i on /etc/hosts when no legacy unit did it. The existing re-assertion relied on starting hosts-guard.service / hosts-bind-mount.service, which do not exist on a fresh machine, so every systemctl cat skipped and the rollback left /etc/hosts with no immutable flag and no bind mount -- strictly less protected than before the rollback.

verification.command: sudo bash linux_configuration/fixes/migrate_hosts_guard_to_guard_lib.sh --rollback --dry-run (pristine vmbox guest, guards installed by install_core_system.sh --all)
verification.evidence: DRYRUN_RC=0, reporting it would uninstall the hosts, nsswitch and resolved instances. Before this change the same command printed 'no rollback state at /var/lib/guard-lib-migration - nothing to roll back to' and exited 1.
ROLLBACK_RC=0. Uninstalled file-guard hosts, nsswitch and resolved, then logged 're-asserted chattr +i on /etc/hosts (no legacy unit to do it)'.

Only shutdown-schedule.conf remains, which belongs to a different feature and must not be touched. /etc/hosts shows ----i----------------- and still holds all 178410 lines; the bind mount is gone, which is the intended post-rollback state.
Clean. An initial A && B || C form was rewritten as if/else after SC2015 pointed out the C branch can run when A succeeds, which matters because `run` is a no-op under --dry-run.

hosts_guard_rollback: 31 passed, 0 failed; whole suite exits 0. The first attempt failed one case: the refusal message is asserted verbatim by test_hosts_guard_rollback.sh:115, and the new no-instance branch had dropped the trailing 'to'. The wording was restored rather than the assertion loosened, since the test is checking the user-visible explanation.

risks: Rollback is now reachable in more situations, so an accidental invocation can unregister live guards. It still refuses when no instance is registered, and it keeps the canonical copy via --keep-canonical, so the file itself is never lost.
The re-assertion only covers /etc/hosts. nsswitch.conf and resolved.conf are left to their plugins, matching the behaviour the migration path already had.
rollback: git revert this commit; the previous behaviour (refuse without a state dir) returns.
After reverting, confirm with sudo bash linux_configuration/fixes/migrate_hosts_guard_to_guard_lib.sh --status that the instance list matches expectations before relying on it.
